messages:
amanda: Hey @eng-runtime team — Marketing needs a verified benchmark bundle for the webinar and launch post. Deliverables: raw CSVs, exact run commands, docker image hash, environment metadata, short methodology blurb, and a 1-line hero stat we can use. Deadline: Wed EOD.

sanjay: Got it. We'll run a focused set. Which hero stat do you prefer (p50 latency or tokens/sec)? Also confirm models/variants.

amanda: Hero: p95 latency for a 64-token dev workflow. Include tokens/sec in the appendix. Models: redwood-1.3b fp16 and int8 quantized. Include streaming on/off and batch sizes 1 and 8.

mike: FYI the previous nightly showed a p95 tail on seq=1024 likely due to prefetch behavior. I'll start a memory-tuned run for long sequences. Recommend 3k samples per config and 200 warmups for stability.

elainE: Note for press: include GPU type and kernel driver + container runtime versions in every metadata file. Also include model checksum.

sanjay: Plan: deterministic tokenization + fixed RNG seed, 3,000 randomized requests per config, 200 warmup requests, export CSV + a small JSON metadata file with the run command, image: sha256:9f1b3c, model_hash: d4f9e8. We'll add a one-paragraph methodology and a one-line copy for the deck.

amanda: Perfect. Also add acceptance criteria for publishing: if re-run numbers deviate >15% from the draft hero stat, flag and call out variance in the post.

lina: Also include a short note about test mix (pct short/medium/long) and whether caching was enabled. Marketing will cite that.

sanjay: No caching across requests unless explicitly noted. Test mix will be 65% <=64, 25% 65-512, 10% >512. I'll annotate CSV files with that info.

mike: Starting CI jobs now. Will run fp16 then int8, streaming toggled after baseline. Using runtime-bench v0.9 with flags:

```
./runtime-bench --model redwood-1.3b --variant fp16 --seq 64 --batch 1 --streaming off --runs 3000 --warmup 200 --seed 42 --out /tmp/bench/redwood-1.3b-fp16-64-b1.csv
```

runtime-ci-bot: job #550900 started by @mike (redwood-1.3b fp16 seq=64 batch=1).

sanjay: Heads up: for int8 runs we'll also capture token-by-token latencies to double-check decode hotspots. That will add ~10% run time but worth it.

amanda: Can you also produce a condensed 3-line CSV (hero rows) for the deck?

sanjay: Will do. Upload location: https://files.internal/redwood/marketing/bench/1780123456-bundle.zip (contains CSVs, metadata JSONs, raw logs, and the —methodology.md).

mike: CI update: job #550900 finished. p50=28ms p95=82ms tokens/s=430 for fp16 seq=64 batch=1. Posting the artifact link.

sanjay: Uploaded int8 artifacts too. Quick note: int8 p95 is 75ms but we saw a 1% spike at 3k on seq=1024. Investigating; likely memory GC on the host.

elainE: If there's host GC we should annotate the log and mark that run as noisy; consider re-run on a clean host.

mike: Re-ran the noisy 1024 configs on a clean node and p95 stabilized within 8% of original. I'll include both raw logs and the rerun CSV with filename suffix "-clean".

amanda: This is great. Two final asks: (1) drop the one-line hero blurb we can paste into the slide, and (2) a one-paragraph methodology we can include in the blog footnotes.

sanjay: Hero blurb: "Redwood-1.3b (fp16) achieves p95=82ms for 64-token dev workflows on A100 (40GB)."

sanjay: Methodology paragraph: "We measured latency with 3,000 randomized requests per configuration following a 200-request warmup. Measurements use deterministic tokenization and a fixed RNG seed. No cross-request caching unless noted; model weights were pinned to hash d4f9e8. Reported p50/p95 and tokens/sec are computed over the full run; raw CSVs and logs are provided for reproducibility."

amanda: Perfect. I'll prep the slide and blog draft. Thanks everyone 680

runtime-ci-bot: job #550912 (rerun seq=1024 clean node) finished. Artifacts: https://files.internal/redwood/marketing/bench/1780123456-bundle.zip

lina: Closing loop: marketing will publish with callouts for noisy hosts and include both baseline and "-clean" runs in the appendix. If anything else comes up ping here.
